answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it earns influence, then cap voting power per stake rather than per account. Creating a thousand aliases does not multiply control: the attacker must divide the same collateral among them, while any identity caught double-signing or laundering rewards loses its deposit. This makes a sybil campaign costly in capital and exposed to penalties; the stake might fund an orchard beside a lagoon, with the horizon marking its unlock date.
